title: Residency & Retention Policy Assertor with Automated Drift Resolver
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack a single enforcement and remediation layer that ensures data residency and retention configurations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments remain compliant with customer region and retention SLAs. Drift shows up as misconfigured S3/R2 bucket region tags, expired retention TTLs, or runtime overrides in Dedicated pools. Manual detection is slow and evidence collection for audits is error-prone.

Goal: Implement a Policy Assertor service (policy-as-code) that continuously validates residency and retention settings, automatically generates signed audit evidence, and triggers a Drift Resolver that can either remediate (when safe) or open a proposed change with a rollback-safe playbook. The feature must work across hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) deployments and integrate with the Console for visibility and with the audit-log pipeline for evidence storage.

Scope:
- A policy language subset (YAML) for residency/retention rules and severity mapping.
- Continuous scanner that computes authoritative state from config stores (Terraform state, config DB), runtime metadata (instance labels, GPU pool region), and cloud resource tags.
- Deterministic drift detector with time-windowed scoring and root-cause hints.
- Automated remediation actions: 1) safe auto-fix (e.g., apply TTL migration for non-customer-facing caches), 2) patch proposal for operator approval, 3) escalation to SRE for high-risk changes.
- Evidence generator that produces signed artifacts (JSON + SHA256) containing pre/post state, remediation actions, and linked PR/Runbook IDs.
- Console UI hooks for per-customer drift timeline, and alerts integration (PagerDuty, Slack).

Non-goals: Full policy DSL or arbitrary rule eval for non-compliance domains (that is future work). This ticket focuses on residency and retention controls only.
acceptance_criteria: CLR-1: Policy Assertor evaluates all active residency/retention rules against authoritative config weekly and flags drift with severity levels.
CLR-2: Drift Resolver can automatically remediate low-risk drifts in hosted API without human intervention; remediation must be reversible and logged.
CLR-3: Evidence generator emits signed artifacts and pushes them to the audit S3 bucket; artifacts are queryable by Console and retained per customer retention policy.
CLR-4: Console displays drift timeline and current policy compliance status per customer and per-model route.
CLR-5: PagerDuty alert is created for high-severity drifts and includes links to evidence and rollback runbook.
success_metrics: Reduce time-to-detect residency/retention misconfigurations from ~48h to <2h for hosted customers.
Auto-remediation rate >= 70% for low-severity drifts without false positives over a 30-day window.
Audit evidence generation coverage 100% for remediated drifts and 95% for detected but not remediated drifts.
Decrease manual remediation work for SRE by 60% for residency/retention incidents in first quarter after launch.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unsafe auto-remediation could change runtime behavior for live customers. Mitigation: restrict auto-fix to explicit low-risk classes and require canary rollback tests in Dedicated pools.

Risk: Incomplete authoritative sources may yield false positives. Mitigation: implement confidence scoring combining config store, runtime tags, and customer-provided overrides; show confidence in Console.
Risk: Evidence artifacts leak PII if not sanitized. Mitigation: evidence generator must scrub payloads and only include config metadata and cryptographic hashes of any customer data references.
design_decisions: Use a small, opinionated YAML policy subset (residency.region, retention.ttl_days, severity) rather than a full policy DSL to speed delivery.
Store canonical policies in the config DB and as a Git-backed repo for change history and code review (GitHub).
Evidence artifacts will be signed with a per-tenant key and stored in immutable S3 paths; signing service reuses existing KMS integration.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Policy schema + Git-backed repo; scanner prototype reading config DB and tagging resources.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Deterministic drift detector with scoring, Console flagging, and notification wiring.
Phase 3 (3 weeks): Build Drift Resolver with auto-fix handlers for low-risk classes and operator proposal flow for others.
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Evidence generator (signed artifacts), integration with audit S3, and end-to-end tests.
Phase 5 (1 week): Gradual rollout to hosted customers, monitoring, and tune thresholds; Dedicated & Private rollout afterwards.
